To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure, electrochemistry and function of thylakoidal membranes are not changed by polycation binding.

(i) the structure and electrostatics of thylakoidal membranes are not affected by PAAH adsorption, and (ii): the efficiency of electron transport in thylaokids is not changed significantly after complex formation.

the polycation interactions are not strong enough to affect the electron transport in thylaoid membranes and the morphology of the built up structures is determined by the properties of polycation molecules and by their interactions with thylakaoids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new functional nanostructures and materials for applications in biotechnology, bioelectronics and nanotechnology.
the study of the structure and properties of hybrid systems composed of biological and synthetic components.
the development of new functional materials for applications in nanobiotechnology and bioelectronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hybrid system composed of thylakoidal membranes and PAAH is a stable and well-defined structure that is capable to preserve the biological activity of thylakodial membranes and can be used in the fabrication of planar functional nanodevices.
polycation binding to thylakioids in the range of concentrations used in this work does not change the structure and functioning of thylaokoid membranes.
the thylakoid/PAAH complex is formed in aqueous bulk phase and on solid substrates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that it is possible to form a complex system from a synthetic polycation (polymer) and biological component (thylakoid membranes) with the preservation of biological activity of the component and without any noticeable changes in the structure and functioning of the biological component.

we have shown the feasibility of the fabrication of complex hybrid systems from biological components and polymers and demonstrated that these systems can be used as building blocks for the construction of complex functional planar nanostructures.
thylakoid membrane is a good model for the study of the effects of polycations on biological membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the thylakoid polycation system can be used as a model for the investigation of the interactions between synthetic polymers and biological membranes, as well as for the fabrication of novel hybrid functional nanostructures.
the hybrid systems composed of biological components, synthetic polymers, and inorganic materials, can be fabricated using the self-assembly approach.
the hybrid systems of thylakoidal membranes and polycations can be considered as promising materials for development of functional nanostructures with controlled properties.
